core_obligations: Write down the square whose fibre product structure identifies i with the base change of Delta_{Z/T} (proof lines 525-532).
Apply the properties of the diagonal to obtain the first assertion (proof lines 532-534).
Read assertions (2), (3) and (4) off the corresponding properties of the diagonal under the three hypotheses on Z -> T (proof lines 534-535).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma, opening with the slogan about the top arrow of a magic diagram: for morphisms f : X -> Z, g : Y -> Z and Z -> T of algebraic spaces over S, the induced morphism i : X x_Z Y -> X x_T Y is representable, locally of finite type, locally quasi-finite, separated and a monomorphism, and becomes an immersion, a closed immersion or quasi-compact under local separatedness, separatedness or quasi-separatedness of Z -> T (source lines 505-522). The proof identifies the defining square as a fibre product, which exhibits i as the base change of the diagonal Delta_{Z/T}; all four assertions then follow from the properties of the diagonal recorded earlier in the chapter and the translation principle for representable morphisms.
